t:
Section 641(e) of the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act of 1996 (division C of Public Law 104–208) is amended—

    (1) in paragraph (1)—

        (A) by striking “an approved institution of higher education and a designated exchange visitor program” and inserting “the Attorney General”; 
        (B) by striking “the time—” and inserting the following: “a time prior to the alien being classified under subparagraph (F), (J), or (M) of section 101(a)(15) of the Immigration and Nationality Act.”; and 
        (C) by striking subparagraphs (A) and (B);  
    (2) by amending paragraph (2) to read as follows:
“(2) Remittance.—The fees collected under paragraph (1) shall be remitted by the alien pursuant to a schedule established by the Attorney General for immediate deposit and availability as described under section 286(m) of the Immigration and Nationality Act.”; 
    (3) in paragraph (3)—

        (A) by striking “has” the first place it appears and inserting “seeks”; and 
        (B) by striking “has” the second place it appears and inserting “seeks to”;  
    (4) in paragraph (4)—

        (A) by inserting before the period at the end of the second sentence of subparagraph (A) the following: “, except that, in the case of an alien admitted under section 101(a)(15)(J) of the Immigration and Nationality Act as an au pair, camp counselor, or participant in a summer work travel program, the fee shall not exceed $40”; and 
        (B) by adding at the end of subparagraph (B) the following new sentence: “Such expenses include, but are not necessarily limited to, those incurred by the Secretary of State in connection with the program under subsection (a).”; and  
    (5) by adding at the end the following new paragraphs:
“(5) Proof of payment.—The alien shall present proof of payment of the fee before the granting of—
“(A) a visa under section 222 of the Immigration and Nationality Act or, in the case of an alien who is exempt from the visa requirement described in section 212(d)(4)
of the Immigration and Nationality Act, admission to the United States; or
“(B) change of nonimmigrant classification under section 248 of the Immigration and Nationality Act to a classification described in paragraph (3).
“(6) Implementation.—The provisions of section 553 of title 5, United States Code (relating to rule-making) shall not apply to the extent the Attorney General determines necessary to ensure the expeditious, initial implementation of this section.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the reference to rule-making under 5 U.S.C. 553 signals a public comment process. But this provision does the opposite: it lets the Attorney General waive notice-and-comment procedures for initial implementation. The rest of the section only concerns fee collection, remittance and proof of payment by aliens, with no consultation, hearing, advisory body or right to sue involving outside parties. The label is uncertain because the waiver is partial and implies rulemaking would otherwise apply.
fable.s: The provisions of section 553 of title 5, United States Code (relating to rule-making) shall not apply to the extent the Attorney General determines necessary to ensure the expeditious, initial implementation of this section.

opus.w: The only reference to rulemaking switches off the notice-and-comment rules of 5 U.S.C. 553, so it removes public input instead of requiring it. The other changes cover fee collection, a payment schedule set by the Attorney General and proof that the alien paid. Like a benefit application, paying a fee is not taking part in a federal decision. No state, expert, company or member of the public is consulted, and no one is given a right to sue.
opus.s: The provisions of section 553 of title 5, United States Code (relating to rule-making) shall not apply to the extent the Attorney General determines necessary to ensure the expeditious, initial implementation of this section.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** The section mentions "section 553 of title 5 ... (relating to rule-making)", the notice-and-comment process. Rulemaking would bring the public in, so this looks like participation.
2. **Why it fails:** The provision does the opposite. It says the notice-and-comment rules "shall not apply" when the Attorney General needs to get the program running quickly, which removes the public's chance to comment. The rest of the section covers fees, a payment schedule the Attorney General sets, and proof of payment. Paying a fee is like applying for a benefit, and no outside party is consulted before any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: The text explicitly states that the rule-making provisions of section 553 of title 5 (which typically require public comment) shall *not* apply. This is an exemption from participation, not a requirement for it. It looks like participation because it mentions "rule-making" in the context of implementation.
qwen_chat.s: “(6) Implementation.—The provisions of section 553 of title 5, United States Code (relating to rule-making) shall not apply to the extent the Attorney General determines necessary to ensure the expeditious, initial implementation of this section.”
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it mentions "rule-making" in the context of implementation.
Resolution: The text explicitly states that the rule-making provisions of section 553 of title 5 (which typically require public comment) shall *not* apply. This is an exemption from participation, not a requirement for it.
